systemParams.title: System parameters
systemParams.pageIntro: Only the super administrator has full remote access to the controller. Settings below cover connectivity and secure remote administration.
systemParams.httpWarning: HTTP connection — traffic is not encrypted. Use HTTPS where possible to protect data.
systemParams.saveSuccess: Settings saved. The controller may reboot.
systemParams.networkIntro: Parameters for accessing the controller from any device (PC, tablet, phone). Set IP, mask, gateway, and port as provided by IT or for your LAN.
systemParams.dhcpHint: With DHCP on, the controller receives IP, mask, and gateway from the network DHCP server. With DHCP off, set a static IP manually.
systemParams.ipHint: Example: 192.168.1.50. Must be unique on the network.
systemParams.gatewayHint: Router or gateway IP. Needed for other subnets and the internet.
systemParams.dns1Hint: For name resolution (NTP, updates). Often same as the gateway.
systemParams.webPortHint: Web UI port (1–65535). Default 8080. Remote URL: http://CONTROLLER_IP:{port}
systemParams.securityIntro: Recommendations to protect the controller from unauthorized access when administrators work remotely.
systemParams.secVpn: VPN: for internet access use corporate VPN. The controller should not be exposed directly to the internet.
systemParams.secLan: Local network: prefer the same subnet as the controller (LAN).
systemParams.secAccounts: Accounts: use strong passwords (min. 8 characters). Change admin passwords regularly.
systemParams.secRoles: Roles: grant minimum privilege. Operators — view only; admins — configuration and system settings.
systemParams.secHttps: HTTPS: enable when supported by firmware to encrypt traffic.
systemParams.secFirewall: Firewall: on the gateway restrict access to the controller to trusted IPs or VPN only.
systemParams.secLimitsBody: connection uses HTTP (not encrypted). For internet access you must use VPN.
systemParams.vpnIntro: VPN is configured on the router or on a PC in the network, not on the controller. After VPN you are on the LAN and can open the WebUI at e.g. 192.168.1.x.
systemParams.vpnRouter: VPN on router: if the router supports WireGuard/OpenVPN, enable the VPN server and create a user. Connect from the remote device, then open the WebUI and enter the controller address.
systemParams.vpnPc: VPN on PC: run a VPN server on the PC hosting the WebUI. On the router, forward the VPN port to that PC.
systemParams.vpnTailscale: Tailscale / ZeroTier: install on a LAN PC and the remote device — encrypted tunnel without router port forwarding.
systemParams.vpnAfter1: Open the WebUI in the browser (PC IP from LAN or VPN).
systemParams.vpnAfter2: Use «Connect to controller» and enter the controller address.
systemParams.vpnDocNote: See REMOTE_TESTING.md, section on remote access over VPN.
systemParams.timeIntro: Correct time is required for the event log. Hostname helps identify the device on the network.
systemParams.ntpHint: Time sync server; enterprises often use internal NTP.
systemParams.hostnameHint: Name for DNS and discovery (e.g. doors-controller-floor1).
systemParams.timezoneHint: For correct times in the event log.
systemParams.timeNote: NTP, hostname, and time zone will be saved when supported by controller firmware.
systemParams.flashIntro: Cleanup of operational flash data: configuration, event log/statistics, and mapping. Service user database is preserved.
systemParams.flashHint: This action is irreversible. MASTER performs reboot after cleanup.
systemParams.flashConfirmText: Are you sure you want to fully clear flash on the controller?\n\nThis will erase configuration, events/statistics, mapping, and users. This action cannot be undone.
systemParams.flashClearSuccess: Flash cleanup started. The controller is rebooting.
systemParams.flashModalIntro: Click “Scan boards”, select target nodes with checkboxes, then clear only selected ones.
systemParams.flashUsersPreservedNote: Users section is service data and is not cleared.
systemParams.flashConfirmServiceSelectedText: Selected boards to clear: {nodes}. Users service section will also be erased. Continue?
systemParams.flashServiceDangerNote: Danger: Users service data will be deleted and may require user re-initialization.

permissions.title: Role permissions
permissions.intro: There are three roles with different access levels. Below is the permission matrix. You can only change other roles’ rights: the super administrator configures Admin and Operator; an administrator configures only Operator.
permissions.levelDescNone: section is hidden from the menu; direct URL shows “access denied”.
permissions.levelDescView: open the section and view data only (monitoring: doors, events, alarms, statistics).
permissions.levelDescChangePassword: mainly for Settings → Profile: user may change only their own password.
permissions.levelDescEdit: open and change settings (configuration, system parameters, profile, permissions). For monitoring, similar to View.
permissions.levelDescManage: full access including create/edit/delete entities (e.g. Users).
permissions.roleSuperAdminDesc: Only the super administrator has full remote access to the controller. They can change rights for Admin and Operator. Their own rights are fixed. System parameters are super-admin only.
permissions.roleAdminDesc: Admin rights are set by Super Admin. An administrator can change permissions only for Operator.
permissions.roleOperatorDesc: Rights are set by Super Admin or Admin. Typically: monitoring view and password change in profile.

content.overview:
After sign-in you see the main screen. The header shows the logo, controller link status (green indicators mean OK, “No connection” when offline; error after three failed polls), and the signed-in user with role. Click the logo to return to the dashboard.

Below are tabs: Monitoring, Configuration (admins), and Settings. Each tab opens a sidebar; the active item is highlighted. Unsaved mapping changes may show a confirmation dialog when leaving.

Monitoring: Doors, Events, Alarms, Statistics. Configuration: Door setup; mapping opens via the Mapping button. Settings: Profile, System parameters, Permissions, Users, Help, About.
content.monitoring_doors:
Doors shows the full table of door states. Auto-refresh about every 5 s.

Filter bar: status (All / Open / Closed / With alarm / Locked), door ID field (ID-1-1 or 1-1), reset filters.

Table columns include board, door, Global ID, sequence, Drawing ID, state, comment, alarm reasons, open time. Read-only.
content.monitoring_events:
Events is the system event log. Auto-refresh about every 10 s when filters are idle.

Filters: event type, door ID, source; reset filters.

Columns include index, time, type, user, door, source, Drawing ID, argument; pagination. Super admins may clear, export, or print the journal.
content.monitoring_alarms: Alarms lists doors with active alarms plus summary counts. Read-only.
content.monitoring_statistics: Statistics shows aggregated system data. Read-only.
content.config_doors:
Door setup is for administrators. Modes: configuration list and editor (tabs: General, Doors, Dependencies, Timeouts). Draft auto-save is available.

From the list: open file, create, load from controller, manage saved configurations.

In the editor: save, apply to controller, mapping, and set RTC time on the system parameters page.
content.config_mapping: Mapping is the graphical door map editor (NAME_map.json). Edit/view modes, wall/door/comment tools, grid, save and upload to the controller. Leaving with unsaved changes asks for confirmation.
content.settings_system: System parameters focus on the super administrator: network (DHCP, static IP, DNS, web port), security and VPN guidance, time (NTP, hostname, time zone), RTC display and sync-with-PC button, and controller info (IP, Node ID, uptime).
content.settings_profile: Profile shows username, role, and an e-mail field stored locally in the browser. User password changes are done under Settings → Users for admins.
content.settings_permissions: Permissions is the Super Admin / Admin / Operator matrix by system section. Levels: none, view, change password, edit, manage. Apply saves the matrix in the browser.
content.settings_users: Users is super-admin only: account table, create, edit, delete (with confirmation).
